subject: QuantWave private deployment — urgent p95 latency & 500-rate spike
messages:
From: ops@quantwave.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: sara@quantwave.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Sudden p95 jump and 500s — Redwood private cluster (eu-west-2)

Markus / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sustained increase in p95 latency for our private VPC deployment starting ~13:45 UTC. Error rate (5xx) has climbed from 0.2% to ~3.6% over the last 30 minutes. This is impacting our inference pipelines for live scoring — downstream batch jobs are backing up.

Quick facts:
- Cluster: quantwave-prod-eu (private)
- Model: rw-instruct-v2-13b-q4 (variant: q4_0)
- Observed: p50 ~120ms (ok), p95 ~1.1s (was 220ms normal), 5xx spike ~3.6% (from 0.2%)
- Recent change: we rolled a small canary of the new batching config at 12:30 UTC (increase max_batch_size -> 64).

Attached: quantwave_metrics_20270209.csv (token/time series) and a replay_profile capturing 12:30-14:00 window.

Can you triage? We need immediate mitigation (fallback, canary rollback, or routing to hosted variant) and a short RCA. Also, if we need an exec sync, loop in whoever is necessary.

— QuantWave SRE
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: ops@quantwave.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 14:21:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump and 500s — Redwood private cluster (eu-west-2)

Thanks for the alert and the attachments. I'm putting Monica and Vivek on the thread to lead the triage.

Immediate items we will run now:
- Check autoscaler and GPU queue lengths, and drain any failing workers.
- Verify if the new batching config is causing KV-cache thrash or forced small-LLM kernel path fallbacks.
- If necessary, we can rollback max_batch_size on the route or route a fraction of traffic to your hosted model variant for stability.

Monica / Vivek — can you confirm ETA for first findings (30 min)? If we see sustained 5xx > 1% at the 30min mark we should request an exec call and propose a temporary credit / SLA remediation.

-Markus
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: ops@quantwave.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 14:46:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump and 500s — Redwood private cluster (eu-west-2)

Quick triage notes after 25m:
- Autoscaler: stable, no noisy OOMs.
- GPU worker logs: intermittent kernel selection warnings for GEMM path on some hosts (lines attached in replay). Looks like a subset of hosts fell back to a slower kernel for long sequences.
- Batcher: the increased max_batch_size caused queues to hold requests longer waiting to fill batches; combined with request-size variance, this increased head-of-line latency. On a few hosts we observed KV-cache eviction churn when batches arrive out-of-order -> CPU contention.
- 5xx source: proxy-level timeouts to the runtime when the worker exceeds its configured request-processing deadline (we saw task timeouts rising).

Mitigation plan (recommended, low-risk):
1) Roll back the canary batching change to previous max_batch_size (48 -> 32) immediately for the route.
2) Apply a short-lived per-host kernel pin for affected hosts to force the optimized GEMM path while we collect debug traces.
3) Enable a temporary route-split: 10% traffic to hosted fallback model in us-west/eu to reduce pressure overnight.

I can push rollback in 10m and provide a before/after replay. ETA to see p95 drop ~10-20m after rollback. If rollback isn't acceptable for QuantWave ops, we'll instead throttle and carve traffic.

Attachments referenced: replay_profile_20270209.pb.gz (sent by QuantWave).

-Monica
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: ops@quantwave.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: sara@quantwave.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump and 500s — Redwood private cluster (eu-west-2)

Monica — thanks, please proceed with rollback now. We need p95 under control before tomorrow's batch window.

Also flagging to Sara (CTO): if this is an internal runtime regression we will request a temporary SLA remediation while we stabilize.

—QuantWave SRE
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: sara@quantwave.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, purchasing@quantwave.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Exec sync proposal — QuantWave private deployment incident (p95 & 5xx)

Sara — following up with a brief exec summary and proposed next steps. We're marking this for an operational review tomorrow.

Summary:
- Incident: Elevated p95 and 5xx observed on private VPC cluster quantwave-prod-eu following a canary change to batching. Root cause appears to be combined effects of batching + kernel fallbacks on a subset of hosts causing CPU contention and request-processing timeouts.
- Impact: Live scoring p95 spiked from ~220ms to ~1.1s; 5xx peaked ~3.6% and is now reduced after rollback. Some downstream backfills delayed.
- Actions taken: Monica rolled back the canary batching change and applied per-host kernel pins; we enabled a 10% route-split to hosted as a pressure relief. Metrics attached show p95 trending down.

Proposed next steps:
1) Host-level RCA with trace/coredump collection for affected hosts (owner: Redwood infra) — target 72h.
2) Model-serving playbook update: add a default throttling policy when max_batch_size changes and require a staged ramp with traffic shaping for private deployments (owner: QuantWave ops + Redwood SRE) — target 2 weeks.
3) Offer a goodwill credit for the incident window and an SLA remediation discussion (owner: Redwood GTM) — propose 10% usage credit for affected period.

We recommend a 30-minute exec sync tomorrow at 09:00 CET to align on RCA scope and remediation timeline. Please let us know availability.

Thanks — happy to jump on the call with technical leads.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
